earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists/comparative notes (Nordenskiold 1905; Rivet 1910; Crequi-Montfort & Rivet 1913; Fleck 2013 overview); no grammar or phonology of Atsahuaca exists.

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, G. de & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne: Le groupe Otuké. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 10(1): 317-337 (transcription key p. 318 n. 2).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Pano paper refers all transcription conventions to this note; it would say what the acute/breve accents on the Atsahuaka forms denote (tonic accent vs. length), which is needed before anyone infers a stress pattern from the wordlist.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the AMNH 99. New York: AMNH.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Atsawaka stress. Lists the entire documentation of †Atsawaka as 'Nordenskiöld (1905: 275-276/1906: 526-527) 49-word list; Créqui-Montfort and Rivet (1913: 46-78) 223-word lexicon collected by Nordenskiöld' (pp. 96-97); Atsawaka/Yamiaka treated as two dialects of one language (p. 12, table 1).

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: Pano-Takana.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Atsawaka appears only in the classification lists (†Atsawaca, Chacobo/southwestern subgroups).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; entry reads 'Atsahuaca or Chaspa - spoken on the Carama River in the same country. [E. Nordenskiöld 1905, pp. 275-276.]' plus a short comparative wordlist.

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, G. de & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne: Les dialectes Pano de Bolivie. Le Muséon n.s. 14: 19-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. Pages 24-41 give notes on genre, nombre, pronoms, suffixes; pp. 41-45 give 'correspondances de voyelles et de consonnes' only; pp. 46-78 the comparative vocabulary in which Atsahuaka ('At', Nordenskiöld's 223-word list) forms carry accent marks (kǎkámǎ 'ananas', héuvi 'arbre', šinosǒko 'grande araignée') whose meaning is referred to a note in their Otuké paper (JSA 10, p. 318 n. 2). No accent rule.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1910. Sur quelques dialectes panos peu connus. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 7: 221-242.
sources.note: The only other primary publication of Nordenskiöld's Atsahuaca/Yamiaca material; would confirm whether Rivet added any remark on accent marks. Per Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913 it only reproduces the vocabularies, so low expected yield.

sources.citation: Nordenskiöld, Erland. 1905. Beiträge zur Kenntnis einiger Indianerstämme des Rio Madre de Dios-Gebietes. Ymer 25: 265-312 (Atsahuaca wordlist pp. 275-276).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement. Only a pronunciation key before the 49-word Atsahuaca column: 'Die Aussprache im allgemeinen wie Spanisch' (p. 275) with s-hacek, ä, w, ö, l explained; forms carry acute accents (páucani 'Ohr', macáni 'Hand', récani 'Nase', hána 'Zunge', umapása 'Wasser', chinapóto 'Asche', huári 'Sonne', óse 'Mond', usáqui 'schlafen', mastára 'schlecht') but their meaning is never stated and no rule is given.

sources.citation: Lyon, Patricia J. 1975. Dislocación tribal y clasificaciones lingüísticas en la zona del río Madre de Dios. Actas del XXXIX Congreso Internacional de Americanistas 5: 185-207. Lima: IEP.
